11 stories from the last 24 hours. Here's what matters today.

Agents

1. Okta buys AI security startup Permiso; source says for about $200M
Okta on Thursday agreed to acquire AI identity security startup Permiso Security , betting that demand for protecting AI agents and other machine identities will grow as enterprises deploy autonomous software across their operations. The identity management company did not disclose the terms of the transaction.
Read more

2. In the Hugging Face breach, OpenAI’s hacker was noisy and fast — but not unstoppable
Earlier this month, AI dataset platform Hugging Face shocked the world when it revealed that it had fallen victim to a fully autonomous AI-powered cyberattack. Days later, the story took another dramatic twist when OpenAI admitted that the hacker behind the breach was one of its AI models , which broke out of a testing environment and into protected Hugging Face systems in an effort to circumvent a benchmark.

5. OpenAI’s accidental cyberattack against Hugging Face is science fiction that happened
The short version: OpenAI were running a cybersecurity test against an unreleased model, with the model’s guardrail features turned off. Rather than solve the test, the model broke its way out of OpenAI’s sandbox, then found exploits to break in to Hugging Face, all so it could cheat on the test by stealing the answers.
